heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Hire employees in Austria without a local entity
heroData.description: Use an Employer of Record to hire talent in Austria compliantly. Bypass the need for a local subsidiary while ensuring full compliance with Austrian Labor Law, including social security, 14th-month salary, and AMS labor leasing specificities.
heroData.bestFor: Companies testing the Austrian market or hiring remote talent fast

steps.title: Service Agreement
steps.description: Sign a framework agreement with the EOR provider. The EOR must hold a valid temporary employment agency license (Überlassung) from the Austrian Public Employment Service (AMS).

steps.title: Employee Data Collection
steps.description: Gather employee details: passport, proof of residence, bank details, and Austrian social security number (Versicherungsnummer). If the employee is new to Austria, initiate social security registration.

steps.title: Employment Contract Drafting
steps.description: Draft a compliant local employment contract (Dienstzettel). Key inclusions: annual salary (split into 14 payments), working hours (max 40h/week), and notice periods.

steps.title: Social Security Registration
steps.description: EOR registers the employee with the regional health insurance fund (ÖGK) before their first day of work. This covers health, pension, accident, and unemployment insurance.

steps.title: Onboarding & IT
steps.description: Employee receives onboarding packet and IT equipment. Austrian law (ArbeitnehmerInnenschutzgesetz) requires ergonomic assessments for remote workers.

items.title: Labor Leasing License (AUG)
items.text: Ensure your EOR has a valid labor leasing license (Gewerbeberechtigung für die Überlassung von Arbeitskräften). Hiring through an unlicensed provider is illegal and carries heavy fines.

items.title: 13th and 14th Month Salary
items.text: In Austria, the 13th (Holiday) and 14th (Christmas) salaries are mandatory under most Collective Bargaining Agreements. These are taxed at a preferential rate of 6%.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: Notice periods are strictly regulated. Employers must typically give at least 6 weeks' notice (increasing with tenure) to the end of a quarter, unless contract specifies 15th/end of month.

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Using an EOR for sales-generating roles or senior management for >18 months effectively may trigger Permanent Establishment (PE) risks for the foreign company.

faqs.question: Can I hide the EOR relationship from the employee?
faqs.answer: No. The employment contract is legally between the EOR and the employee. The employee must understand this tripartite relationship.

faqs.question: Is the 13th/14th salary included in the negotiated annual gross?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. An 'All-In' contract must specify the base salary and the bonus separate components. Standard practice is to negotiate an annual gross which is paid out 14 times.

faqs.question: How does termination work with an EOR?
faqs.answer: Termination requires strict adherence to notice periods (often 6 weeks+). Review by the Works Council may be needed. Severance pay (Abfertigung Neu) is handled via a monthly contribution (1.53%) to a staff provision fund.

steps.title: Data Aggregation (15th - 20th)
steps.description: Collect changes: new hires, terminations, variable pay (commissions), sick leave (Krankenstand), and overtime hours. Austrian law requires strict overtime tracking.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation (20th - 25th)
steps.description: Apply tax brackets (0% to 55%), social security deductions, and calculate the 1/14th split for special payments.

steps.title: Reporting & Filing (End of Month)
steps.description: Submit monthly contribution report (mBGM) to the Health Insurance Fund. Payment of social security contributions is due by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Wage Tax Payment
steps.description: Remit Wage Tax (Lohnsteuer) and Municipal Tax (Kommunalsteuer) to the respective tax office and municipality by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Distribute digital payslips to employees. Ensure 'Lohnzettel' (annual playslip) is generated at year-end.

items.title: The 'Jahressechstel'
items.text: The 13th and 14th salaries are taxed at a flat rate of 6% (after a small exemption), provided they do not exceed 1/6th of total annual income. This is a key benefit for employees.

items.title: Submission Deadlines
items.text: Failing to submit the mBGM report by the end of the month or paying taxes by the 15th results in immediate surcharges (Säumniszuschlag).

items.title: Commuter Allowance (Pendlerpauschale)
items.text: Employees traveling designated distances to work are entitled to tax deductions. This must be processed through payroll.

items.title: Union Agreements (Kollektivvertrag)
items.text: 98% of Austrian jobs are covered by a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). These dictate minimum salaries and annual increases.

faqs.question: What is the 13th and 14th salary?
faqs.answer: It is a standard bonus payment equal to one month's salary, paid in June (Holiday Bonus) and November (Christmas Bonus). It is mandatory under almost all CBAs.

faqs.question: Are there payroll taxes on benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes. Benefits-in-kind (Sachbezug) such as company cars or free parking are taxable. Zero-emission vehicles are exempt from benefit-in-kind tax.

faqs.question: How are sick days handled?
faqs.answer: Employers must continue paying full salary for at least 6 weeks (Entgeltfortzahlung), after which the health insurance fund takes over partial payments.

items.title: 13th & 14th Salary
items.text: Don't forget to factor in the Holiday (June) and Christmas (Nov) bonuses. These are taxed at a preferential rate (6%) but add two full months of gross salary to the annual cost.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: For 2025/2026, the maximum monthly contribution base (Höchstbeitragsgrundlage) is approx. €6,450. Contributions are capped at this level.

items.title: Total Load Estimate
items.text: As a rule of thumb, budget roughly 30-31% on top of the annual gross salary (including 13/14th payments) to cover all employer non-wage labor costs.

steps.title: Determine Gross Monthly Salary
steps.description: Agree on a monthly gross amount (Bruttogehalt) generally paid 14 times a year.

steps.title: Add Non-Wage Labor Costs
steps.description: Add ~30% for social security (Dienstgeberanteil), municipal tax, and other levies.

steps.title: Check Commuter Allowance
steps.description: If applicable, the 'Pendlerpauschale' reduces the tax base but doesn't cost the employer extra directly; however, it must be processed in payroll.

steps.title: Annualize
steps.description: Multiply monthly total cost by 14 (or 12 + 2 bonus payments) to get the true annual cost of employment.

faqs.question: Is the 13th/14th salary mandatory?
faqs.answer: It is not statutory by law but mandated by almost all Collective Bargaining Agreements (Kollektivvertrag), effectively making it mandatory.

faqs.question: What is the 'Dienstgeberabgabe'?
faqs.answer: A specific tax for specialized employees/freelancers, ensuring they contribute to the system if not fully employed. Less common for standard employees.

faqs.question: How are overtime payments taxed?
faqs.answer: The first 10 overtime hours per month get a tax-free allowance up to €86. Generally, overtime is expensive due to surcharges (50% or 100%).

heroData.title: Incorporation in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Setup a GmbH in Austria
heroData.description: Establish a robust presence in the DACH region. A GmbH offers liability protection and strong reputational value, though setup requires notarization and capital deposit.

steps.title: Articles of Association
steps.description: Draft the 'Gesellschaftsvertrag'. It must include company name, seat, business purpose, and share capital details. Must be notarized.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Open a business bank account and deposit the minimum share capital (€10,000 for standard GmbH). Bank issues a confirmation certificate.

steps.title: Notary Appointment
steps.description: Shareholders and Managing Directors sign the deed of incorporation in front of an Austrian notary. Remote signing is possible via specific digital notary procedures.

steps.title: Commercial Registry
steps.description: Notary submits documents to the Firmenbuch (Commercial Register). Registration fee is ~€350. Approval typically takes 1-2 weeks.

steps.title: Tax & Trade Registration
steps.description: Register with the Tax Office (Finanzamt) for a VAT number and apply for a trade license (Gewerbeberechtigung) with the local authority.

items.title: Corporate Tax Rate 2025
items.text: The Corporate Income Tax (Körperschaftsteuer) rate is 23%. This was reduced from 25% in previous years to boost competitiveness.

items.title: Start-up Aid Act (NeuFöG)
items.text: New businesses can apply for NeuFöG status to waive certain government fees and taxes involved in incorporation. Check eligibility with the Chamber of Commerce.

items.title: Trade License (Gewerbeschein)
items.text: Almost every business activity requires a trade license. A Managing Director (gewerberechtlicher Geschäftsführer) must be appointed who meets qualification criteria for regulated trades.

items.title: Managing Director Residency
items.text: Third-country nationals appointed as Managing Directors may need a residence permit if they plan to stay in Austria longer than visa-free allowance.

faqs.question: Can a foreign company own 100% of an Austrian GmbH?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is fully permitted. The shareholder can be a foreign legal entity.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a registered office address in Austria (Sitz). A simple PO Box is not sufficient, but a virtual office with mail forwarding usually suffices.

faqs.question: What is the difference between GmbH and AG?
faqs.answer: GmbH is a private liability company (simpler, €10k capital). AG is a public stock corporation (complex, €70k capital, supervisory board required). GmbH is the standard choice.

heroData.title: Staffing in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Recruit top talent in the DACH region
heroData.description: Austria offers a highly skilled, German-speaking workforce. Recruitment agencies are essential for navigating the tight labor market and strict labor leasing (Arbeitskräfteüberlassung) regulations.
heroData.bestFor: Sourcing specialized roles or volume hiring

steps.title: Requirements Engineering
steps.description: Define the role profile. Note that Austrian job ads MUST state the minimum collective agreement salary (Glleichbehandlungsgesetz), though actual pay is usually higher.

steps.title: Agency Selection
steps.description: Choose a specialized agency. Ensure they understand your industry (e.g., IT, Engineering). Sign Terms of Business regarding exclusivity and replacement guarantees.

steps.title: Sourcing & Screening
steps.description: Agencies use active sourcing (LinkedIn) and local job boards (Karriere.at). Candidates expect a formal interview process.

steps.title: Works Council Hearing
steps.description: If a Works Council exists, you must inform them of the intended hire/grading before the contract is signed.

steps.title: Offer & Contract
steps.description: Issue the 'Dienstzettel'. Be prepared for a 1-month notice period from the candidate's current employer (usually to end of month).

items.title: Salary Transparency Law
items.text: All job advertisements must state the minimum salary according to the applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement. Failing to do so can result in administrative fines.

items.title: Probation Periods
items.text: The statutory maximum probation period is 1 month. This is very short compared to other countries (e.g., Germany's 6 months), so initial screening is critical.

items.title: CV Format
items.text: Austrian CVs are typically detailed ('Lebenslauf'), reverse chronological, and often include a professional photo and date of birth.

faqs.question: What is the standard replacement guarantee?
faqs.answer: Most agencies offer a free replacement if the candidate leaves within the probation period (1 month) or sometimes up to 3 months for senior roles.

faqs.question: Are background checks common?
faqs.answer: Criminal record checks ('Strafregisterbescheinigung') are common for sensitive roles but require candidate consent. Credit checks are rare except for finance roles.

faqs.question: Do I need a license to hire temporary staff?
faqs.answer: You don't need a license to HIRE temp staff, but the agency supplying them MUST have a labor leasing license (Überlassungsgewerbe).

heroData.title: HRIS in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Digitize HR in a compliant manner
heroData.description: Austria has strict requirements for time tracking and data privacy. Your HRIS choice must support Works Council rights and mandatory working hour records.

steps.title: Compliance Check
steps.description: Verify the system supports Austrian specificities: § 26 AZG time tracking, 14 salary split, and GDPR data residency (ideally EU servers).

steps.title: Works Council Consultation
steps.description: If a Works Council exists, introducing an HRIS often requires a company agreement (Betriebsvereinbarung), especially if performance or behavior can be monitored.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Migrate master data (Stammdaten). Ensure historical data for holiday accruals (Urlaubsanspruch) is transferred accurately (25 days/year).

steps.title: Configuration
steps.description: Configure absence types: Sick leave (needs doctor's note upload), Care leave (Pflegefreistellung), and Parental leave (Karenz).

steps.title: Rollout & Training
steps.description: Train employees on time tracking obligations. It is the employer's duty to ensure working hours are recorded correctly.

items.title: Mandatory Time Tracking (§ 26 AZG)
items.text: Employers MUST record start time, end time, and breaks for all employees. 'Trust-based working hours' without recording is largely illegal except for C-level execs.

items.title: Works Council Rights
items.text: Systems that use AI or algorithms to evaluate employees effectively require Works Council consent. Transparency is key.

items.title: Holiday Accrual
items.text: Statutory holiday is 5 weeks (25 days). After 25 years of service, it increases to 6 weeks. Your HRIS must handle this automatic increase.

faqs.question: Can I use a US-based HRIS?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is GDPR compliant (Standard Contractual Clauses or Data Privacy Framework). However, US systems often lack specific fields for Austrian tax classes and religion (for church tax).

faqs.question: Is biometric time tracking allowed?
faqs.answer: Generally, no, unless there is a very high security requirement. Fingerprint scanning for general attendance is usually considered excessive by data protection authorities.

faqs.question: How long must data be kept?
faqs.answer: Payroll data must be kept for 7 years. Time tracking records should be kept for at least 1 year, but practically longer for potential claims.

heroData.title: Accounting in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Financial reporting & tax compliance
heroData.description: Austrian accounting standards (UGB) differ from IFRS. Companies require monthly bookkeeping, VAT filings (UVA), and annual financial statements compliant with Austrian law.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
steps.description: Digitize and submit all invoices and expense receipts. Austria requires 'Ordnungsmäßigkeit der Buchführung' (orderly bookkeeping).

steps.title: VAT Returns (UVA)
steps.description: Submit Preliminary VAT Return (Umsatzsteuervoranmeldung) monthly by the 15th of the second following month (or quarterly if turnover < €100k).

steps.title: Annual Closing
steps.description: Prepare the 'Jahresabschluss' (Financial Statements) within 9 months of year-end. This involves reconciliation of accounts, accruals, and inventory valuation.

steps.title: Tax Filing
steps.description: Submit Corporate Income Tax return (Körperschaftsteuererklärung) electronically via FinanzOnline.

steps.title: Commercial Register Filing
steps.description: Submit the annual financial statements to the Firmenbuch within 9 months. Failure leads to automatic fines (minimum €700).

items.title: Audit Thresholds
items.text: A statutory audit is mandatory if two of three limits are exceeded for two consecutive years: €5M turnover, €2.5M balance sheet total, or 50 employees.

items.title: UGB vs IFRS
items.text: Local statutory accounts must be prepared under Austrian UGB (Unternehmensgesetzbuch), which tends to be more prudent/conservative than IFRS.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: The fiscal year usually matches the calendar year, but a deviate fiscal year (Rumpfwirtschaftsjahr) can be chosen upon incorporation.

faqs.question: Can I keep my books in English?
faqs.answer: Internal records can be in English, but the official submission to the Tax Office and Commercial Register must be in German.

faqs.question: What is a Fiscal Representative?
faqs.answer: Non-EU companies doing taxable business in Austria without a permanent establishment must appoint a Fiscal Representative to handle VAT obligations.

faqs.question: Are digital receipts accepted?
faqs.answer: Yes, scanned receipts are fully accepted provided they are legible and stored securely (GoBD equivalent standards apply).

steps.title: Trade License Check
steps.description: Verify if your business activity is a 'Regulated Trade' (reglementiertes Gewerbe) requiring specific qualifications or a 'Free Trade'. Register with the GISA.

steps.title: Beneficial Owner Register
steps.description: Report Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO) to the defined register (WiEReG) within 4 weeks of incorporation to comply with AML laws.

steps.title: Whistleblower Channel
steps.description: Companies with 50+ employees must establish an internal reporting channel under the Whistleblower Protection Act (HSchG).

steps.title: GDPR Audit
steps.description: Appoint a Data Protection Officer if required. Document Processing Activities (Verarbeitungsverzeichnis) and ensure website cookie banners are compliant.

steps.title: Safety & Health
steps.description: Appoint a Safety Officer (Sicherheitsvertrauensperson) if you have >10 employees. Conduct mandatory workplace risk assessments.

items.title: GDPR Fines
items.text: The Austrian Data Protection Authority (DSB) is active. Non-compliance can lead to fines up to €20M or 4% of global turnover. Google Analytics use has faced scrutiny.

items.title: Whistleblowing (HSchG)
items.text: The HinweisgeberInnenschutzgesetz protects whistleblowers reporting breaches of EU law. The internal channel must ensure confidentiality and allow anonymous reporting.

items.title: Lobbying Register
items.text: Companies engaging in lobbying activities must register in the Lobbying Register to ensure transparency.

items.title: Waste Management
items.text: Packaging compliance (Verpackungsverordnung) requires companies putting packaging on the market to participate in a collection scheme (e.g., ARA).

items.title: Works Council Co-Determination
items.text: The Works Council has strong rights (Mitbestimmung). In some cases (e.g., disciplinary transfers, intrusive IT systems), their consent is legally required.

items.title: E-Government
items.text: Austria's 'Unternehmensserviceportal' (USP) is the central gateway for most compliance filings. Get your ID Austria login sorted early.

faqs.question: Is a physical compliance officer required?
faqs.answer: For regulated sectors (banking, insurance), yes. For general business, a Managing Director often assumes the 'Gewerberechtlicher Geschäftsführer' role.

faqs.question: How strictly is the Trade License enforced?
faqs.answer: Very strictly. Operating without a license (Pfusch) is an administrative offense and competitors can sue for unfair competition.

faqs.question: What are the rules for managing directors?
faqs.answer: The Managing Director (Handelsrechtlicher Geschäftsführer) is personally liable for tax and social security payments if the company defaults due to negligence.

rows.label: R&D Cash Premium (Forschungsprämie)
values: On eligible R&D expenses, paid in cash

rows.label: Loss Carryforward
values: Can offset max 75% of annual profit

rows.label: Group Taxation
values: Offset losses of subsidiaries against parent profit

items.title: Group Taxation Regime
items.text: Austria's Group Taxation (Gruppenbesteuerung) is one of the most attractive in Europe. It allows cross-border loss utilization from non-Austrian subsidiaries under certain conditions.

items.title: Advance Tax Payments
items.text: CIT is prepaid in quarterly installments (Feb, May, Aug, Nov). Cash flow planning must account for these prepayments based on the previous year's profit.

items.title: R&D Premium Application
items.text: The 14% R&D premium is NOT a tax deduction but a cash refund. It requires a detailed expert opinion (Gutachten) from the FFG (Research Promotion Agency).

faqs.question: When is the annual tax return due?
faqs.answer: Generally by June 30th of the following year if filed electronically via FinanzOnline. Extensions via a tax advisor are possible.

faqs.question: Does Austria have a Wealth Tax?
faqs.answer: No, Austria does not levy a general wealth tax on assets, though real estate tax is applicable.

faqs.question: What is the Capital Gains Tax?
faqs.answer: For corporations, capital gains are treated as ordinary income and taxed at the 23% CIT rate. Participation exemptions often apply for sale of shares.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Contractual frameworks for Austria
heroData.description: Drafting valid Master Service Agreements requires attention to Austrian Civil Code (ABGB) and consumer protection laws if applicable. Liability limitations have specific statutory bounds.

steps.title: Choice of Law
steps.description: Explicitly state Austrian Law as governing law. For B2B, this is standard. Courts (Handelsgericht) in Vienna are experienced in commercial disputes.

steps.title: Liability Clauses
steps.description: Define liability caps. Note: Under Austrian law, liability for 'Intent' (Vorsatz) and 'Gross Negligence' (Grobe Fahrlässigkeit) cannot be excluded.

steps.title: Payment Terms
steps.description: Standard payment terms are 14-30 days. The Late Payment Directive allows statutory interest and recovery costs for B2B delays.

steps.title: IP Transfer
steps.description: Clearly define when Intellectual Property rights transfer (usually upon full payment). Moral rights (Urheberpersönlichkeitsrecht) remain with the creator but can be waived.

steps.title: Termination
steps.description: Specify valid reasons for 'Extraordinary Termination' (wichtiger Grund), which allows immediate cancellation regardless of term.

items.title: General Terms & Conditions (AGB)
items.text: If your MSA refers to GTCs, they must be proven to have been 'brought to the attention' of the other party before signing. Hidden clauses (überraschende Klauseln) are void.

items.title: Electronic Signatures
items.text: Qualified Electronic Signatures (QES) e.g., via ID Austria or DocuSign (QES level) are legally equivalent to handwritten signatures for most commercial contracts.

items.title: Cost Reimbursement
items.text: In litigation, the losing party generally pays the court fees and the winner's legal costs (based on the statutory tariff RATG).

items.title: Laesio Enormis
items.text: A contract can be challenged if the value of goods/services is less than half of the consideration paid (verkürzung über die hälfte). In B2B, this is often explicitly excluded.

items.title: Sittenwidrigkeit
items.text: Contracts deemed 'contrary to good morals' are void. This includes excessively long binding periods or usurious interest rates.

items.title: Language
items.text: While English contracts are common in B2B, submitting them to court requires a certified German translation. It is wise to have a bilingual version.

faqs.question: Can we agree on US law for an Austrian client?
faqs.answer: Yes, in B2B. However, mandatory Austrian overriding mandatory provisions (Eingriffsnormen) may still apply, and enforcement can be complex.

faqs.question: Is a non-compete enforceable?
faqs.answer: Yes, but strictly limited in time (max 1 year typically) and scope. For employees, compensation must be paid during the non-compete period.

faqs.question: What is the statute of limitations?
faqs.answer: General statute of limitations is 3 years for claims for goods/services, and 30 years for other rights. Claims for damages expire after 3 years from knowledge.

heroData.title: Software Solutions in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Local & Integrated Tech Stack
heroData.description: The Austrian market relies heavily on localized software for payroll (Lohnverrechnung) and accounting due to specific legal requirements. DATEV and BMD are market leaders.

items.title: Localization is Critical
items.text: Generic global ERPs often fail to handle Austrian specifics like the 13th/14th salary split or local travel expense allowances (Diäten) without expensive customization.

items.title: Electronic Data Transmission
items.text: Ensure your payroll software supports 'ELDA' (Elektronischer Datenaustausch) for mandatory reporting to social security authorities.

items.title: Cloud vs. On-Premise
items.text: While cloud adoption is growing (e.g., Personio), many traditional Austrian firms still prefer on-premise or hosted solutions (e.g., BMD) for perceived data sovereignty.

steps.title: Identify Mandatory Integrations
steps.description: Check for FinanzOnline and ELDA interfaces. Without these, manual administrative burden increases significantly.

steps.title: Check Collective Agreement Support
steps.description: Austrian wages are heavily regulated by 'Kollektivvertrag'. The software should support automatic updates to minimum wage tables.

steps.title: Data Hosting Compliance
steps.description: Ensure the provider hosts data within the EU/EEA to comply with strict GDPR interpretations by Austrian authorities.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks or Xero in Austria?
faqs.answer: It is difficult. They lack native support for Austrian VAT returns (UVA) and specific payroll rules. Local solutions or localized NetSuite/SAP are better.

faqs.question: What is 'Registrierkassenpflicht'?
faqs.answer: The requirement for electronic cash registers with a tamper-proof signature for cash businesses. Your POS software must be compliant.

faqs.question: Is e-invoicing mandatory?
faqs.answer: For B2G (Business to Government) transactions, e-invoicing via USP (Unternehmensserviceportal) is mandatory.

heroData.title: Marketing Agencies in Austria
heroData.subtitle: Creative & Digital Partners
heroData.description: Austria's marketing landscape is centered in Vienna, with a strong focus on high-quality B2B communications and localized DACH strategies.

items.title: DACH Strategy
items.text: Campaigns often run across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland (DACH). However, Austrian German has distinct vocabulary and cultural nuances—localize, don't just copy German content.

items.title: Privacy First
items.text: Austrians are privacy-conscious. 'Cold calling' and aggressive email marketing without double opt-in are strictly regulated and culturally frowned upon.

items.title: Quality Over Quantity
items.text: The market appreciates high production value and certifications (e.g., 'Google Partner'). Trust is a major currency in Austrian business relationships.

steps.title: Define Scope & Region
steps.description: Decide if you need a Vienna-centric campaign or regional reach. Local dialects can vary significantly in urgency and tone.

steps.title: Check References
steps.description: Ask for case studies specifically within the Austrian market. Experience in Germany does not always translate 1:1.

steps.title: Review Contracts
steps.description: Ensure clear IP transfer clauses for creative assets. Agency contracts often default to usage rights rather than full ownership transfer.

faqs.question: What are standard agency rates?
faqs.answer: Daily rates for senior consultants typically range from €1,000 to €1,800. Junior roles/execution can be €500-€800.

faqs.question: Is LinkedIn popular in Austria?
faqs.answer: Yes, for B2B it is the dominant platform. XING is still present but declining compared to LinkedIn.

faqs.question: Do I need a local website domain (.at)?
faqs.answer: Highly recommended. A .at domain signals local presence and significantly builds trust with Austrian consumers and SEO.
